head: claude/phase-h-decision-roundtrip
title: Phase H: decisions answerable from the UI (the decision round-trip)
body:
# Phase H — the control half: decisions answerable from the UI

Operating-layer **Phase H**, per `docs/design/operating-layer-build-plan-DESIGN.md`. **Draft — the manager owns the merge.**

The model puts *"anything waiting on the operator, at the top"* of the dashboard and requires decisions to be answerable **from the UI**, *"so the operator is not the bottleneck on their own decisions."* The measured constraint is **DECISION**. This is the route pair that acts on it.

The SPA side is a separate change in `ict-trader-dashboard` (see the blocker note at the bottom).

---

## ⚠️ First: a precondition my brief said was met is NOT met, and it changed what I built

My brief said *"Your preconditions are MET as of 22:53Z"*, citing #10682. Checked against `WO-20260901-PHASE-H.blocked_on` rather than accepted:

| Precondition | State |
|---|---|
| `WO-20260901-PHASE-B` | `waiting`, not `done`. But the **condition** the edge names — *"the control half extends the read view"* — holds: dashboard #210 merged and the Work section renders. Proceeding, per Phase B's own correction that **an edge must name the CONDITION, never the object that happened to create it**. |
| `BL-…-DB-EXPLORER-IS-UNGATED…` | #10682 **merged** (`0e90202f`). Its own `done_condition (a)` needs the narrowed route **deployed and re-probed**; **a merge is not a deploy**, so the row is open. Not load-bearing for this PR. |
| `BL-…-RETIRE-ANDROID-AND-STREAMLIT-FROM-THE-LIVE-FEED` | **NOT met.** Streamlit's retirement sits on an **unopened** `ict-trader-dashboard` branch (`claude/phase-h-preconditions-retire-streamlit`), and Android was deliberately untouched (that repo is ON ICE). |

**So the read gate is NOT in this PR, and that is a decision rather than an omission.** The design says archiving the other two consumers is *"what makes that tractable — there is nothing else left to keep working."* Streamlit is still live. Attaching `require_session` to the read surface now would take the operator's dashboard down to satisfy a checklist. **Instead I authored the sequencing question as the first real content of the decision channel this PR ships** — so the operator answers it from the UI, which is the point of the phase.

## What this ships

| | |
|---|---|
| `src/runtime/work_decisions.py` | **new** — the transit contract and the four answer states. One owner; the router never re-derives either. |
| `src/web/api/routers/work.py` | `GET /api/bot/work/decisions` (the inbox) · `POST /api/bot/work/decision` (submit one answer) |
| `scripts/ops/commit_work_decisions.py` | **new** — the committer that turns a submission into truth |
| `.github/workflows/work-decision-commit.yml` | **new** — its runner (cron every 2h at :35 + dispatch) |
| `src/web/api/routers/diag.py` | one allowlist entry, `work_decision_transit` |
| `scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py` | one contract, `work_decisions.answer_state` |
| `docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260901-PHASE-H.yaml` | the phase object → `in_flight`, plus the **first real decision request** and a true `operator_decision` edge |
| `CLAUDE.md` · `docs/api-tier-policy.md` · `docs/claude/work/README.md` · `docs/github-actions-workflows.md` · `claude-run-failure-alert.yml` | docs + registrations |
| `tests/test_work_decisions.py` | **new**, 28 tests |

## The contract, which is the whole design

**The repo is the source of truth; the live layer holds no truth at rest** (`operating-layer-schema-and-state-DESIGN.md` § 2). So:

1. The **question** lives in the repo — `decision_requests[]` on a work object, paired with a `blocked_on` edge of `kind: operator_decision`.
2. The operator answers in the SPA → `POST /api/bot/work/decision` appends **one row** to `runtime_logs/work_decision_transit.jsonl`. **Nothing is decided.** The response says `answerState: in_transit`, **never** `committed`.
3. `GET /api/bot/work/decisions` grades it `in_transit` — an **open window**, listable with its age.
4. The committer writes the `answer` block into the object file and it lands as a PR.
5. **Only now** does it grade `committed`.

⚠️ **`committed` is derived from the REPO, never from a flag in the transit log**, and that is deliberate rather than incidental. A `state` column there would be a second, drifting record of a fact the repo already holds — and a lost commit would *look* answered. Reading it off the object file makes the contract structural:

> **Transit fails BACK, never forward.** An answer that does not reach the repo leaves its question **unanswered** — never "answered", never ambiguous. *A question wrongly shown as answered is a decision nobody made.*

### Four answer states, never collapsed

`not_submitted` · `in_transit` · `committed` · `unreadable`. Registered with `collapsed-state-guard` as `work_decisions.answer_state`.

The pair that matters is **`unreadable` vs `not_submitted`**. Collapsing them would report *"we could not read the channel"* as *"the operator has not answered"* — putting a question back on the operator they may already have answered, and making a broken channel indistinguishable from a quiet one. That is `exit_anchor.py`'s `deferred`/`no_anchor` distinction applied to a write path. ⚠️ `committed` is checked **first**, so a decision already made survives an unreadable log: it cannot be un-made by a read failure.

Three more distinctions the envelope keeps apart, each for a stated reason:

- **`awaitingOperator` vs `awaitingCommit`.** An `in_transit` question is also unanswered, but it is waiting on a **committer**, not on the operator. Pooling them would put work on the operator's plate that is not theirs.
- **`transit.state` `absent` vs `unreadable`.** An append-only log never written genuinely holds nothing — a positive reading. One we could not open is not.
- **`unanswerableOperatorEdges`.** A `blocked_on` edge of `kind: operator_decision` carrying **no answerable request** — a question the operator is blocking on and *cannot answer from the UI, because nobody wrote it down*. Surfaced separately, because folding it in with the answerable ones would hide exactly that gap.

## The write gate — a new write surface on a public API

`POST /api/bot/work/decision` copies **`prop.py::_require_write_token`'s polarity verbatim: token-gated and FAIL-CLOSED — 503 when `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` is unset**, rather than accepting an anonymous write. Deliberately **not** the permissive `devices` shape and **not** `learning/progress`'s unauthenticated one: that route is unauthenticated because it carries no secret and no trading impact, whereas an anonymous decision write would let anyone on the internet answer a question **in the operator's name** on a public, browser-reachable host.

It also refuses: an option the author never declared (400) · an empty submission (400 — the same rule `board-post.yml` applies to a blank comment: a vacuous answer that reads as compliance is worse than none) · a traversing `object_id` (400) · unknown object/request (404) · **a request already carrying an `answer` (409** — a committed decision is changed by editing the repo, never by queueing a second answer behind one that landed). A write that fails to persist is a **503, never a 200**.

`writeGate.state` (`open` / `closed_no_token` / `unknown`) is published on the **read** route so the SPA can render *"answering is closed"* instead of a submit button that 503s. The token's value is never echoed.

## Why the committer and its workflow are in this PR and not a follow-up

**A writer with no committer is worse than no writer** — the operator would answer into a void, which is the forward failure the contract exists to refuse. And the precedent is measured: `scripts/ops/work_digest.py` shipped with **no trigger** and appeared in **0 of 125 workflow files**, so it could not have fired.

The workflow reuses `vm-diag-snapshot.yml`'s exact read path (SSH + `curl` against `127.0.0.1:8001/api/diag/log_file`) — **no new network path, no new credential, one READ of one log** — then `commit-to-main` with `verify-merged`, because *"the PR opened"* is not *"the decision landed"*.

⚠️ **DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED.** A scheduled workflow in this repo is not evidence that it fires: `probes.yml` and `due-list.yml` are merged, enabled, syntactically correct and have **never once** fired on cron (`OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON`). A `workflow_dispatch` run is **not** a cron run. ⚠️ **The SSH+curl step is unverifiable from a sandbox** — this session has no VM egress — so it is proven by shape (copied from a working workflow), not by a run. ⚠️ Most runs will commit nothing, and that is correct: a committer that only runs when something is waiting is indistinguishable from one that has broken.

## Population, measured

**Measured 2026-09-01 over the whole store (population = every `*.yaml` under `docs/claude/work/objects/`, n = 584):**

- **0 objects declared a `decision_requests` block.**
- **0 objects carried a `blocked_on` edge of `kind: operator_decision`.**

So the inbox this phase ships was **empty by construction** — the same shape as Phase D, where the machinery landed and the input had not been written. *A decision channel with no questions in it is deployed, not working.* Following Phase A's precedent (*the store's first content is the plan to build the store*), `WO-20260901-PHASE-H` now carries **one real question with four options** — the read-gate sequencing above — plus the true `operator_decision` edge for it. The inbox reads `requestCount: 1`, `awaitingOperator: 1`.

WIP: the phase object moved `dormant → in_flight`, taking the store to **3 of a ceiling of 8** (`check_wip_ceiling.py` verdict `ok`).

## Validation

- **`tests/test_work_decisions.py` — 28 passed.** `tests/test_work_router.py` + `test_work_digest.py` — 42 passed. Related web/diag suites — **321 passed**.
- **Guards: 49 PASS / 17 skipped / 0 fail.** (`layer-guard` first reported `exited 127` — `lint-imports` was absent from the sandbox, not a finding. Installed and run: **6 contracts kept, 0 broken.**)
- **Three guards failed correctly and were fixed, not silenced:** `unwired-artifact-guard` (the committer had no runner → the workflow), `workflow-catalog` + `cron-failure-watch` (the workflow was unregistered → catalogued and added to `claude-run-failure-alert`), and `test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence` (the new log name was undocumented in `CLAUDE.md`).

**The falsifier, stated precisely rather than flatteringly.** All 28 tests fail against the pre-change router — but as a fixture `AttributeError`, which proves the routes are new and **not** that each assertion independently discriminates. So I mutation-tested the two load-bearing invariants instead:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| collapse `unreadable` into `not_submitted` in `grade_answer_state` | `test_unreadable_transit_is_not_reported_as_not_submitted` **FAILS** (1 failed, 27 passed) |
| make the write route return `answerState: committed` | `test_submit_then_commit_is_the_whole_contract` **FAILS** (1 failed, 27 passed) |

The write-gate test carries its own positive control: it asserts **401 with the token SET and 200 with the right bearer**, so the 503-when-unset assertion cannot pass for the trivial reason that the route is broken for every caller.

## Two stale claims in `CLAUDE.md` corrected on the way (field beats comment)

Both on the `/api/bot/work` row, both stale **in the dangerous direction**, both inside this change's blast radius:

1. *"`wip.enforced` is `false` … enforcement ships in Phase C"* — Phase C **merged**; `check_wip_ceiling.py` fails CI on a ninth `in_flight` object. The row told a reader a limit binding their CI was advisory — the same drift the route's own comments record the SPA rendering to the operator's screenshot.
2. *"the store holds the operating-layer build's own 8 phases and nothing else … the ~572 carried rows migrate in Phase C"* — both halves false: **584 objects, 577 `dormant` / 3 `in_flight` / 4 `waiting`.**

## What is NOT in this PR

- **The read gate.** Precondition unmet; see the top. The sequencing is now a live question in the decision inbox.
- **The SPA.** `ict-trader-dashboard` — separate change.
- The 64 CI guards' logic and the provenance layer (build plan § *"What is NOT built"*). Untouched.
- No `config/`, no order path, no VM mutation.

## ⚠️ For the manager

1. **Merging this deploys a new write route.** It is fail-closed, so with `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN` unset in the web-api unit it serves **503** and answers cannot be submitted at all. Whether to set it is an operator decision, not mine — and until it is set, `writeGate.state` reads `closed_no_token`, which the SPA renders as *answering is closed*, not as an outage.
2. **The workflow's SSH step has not been run.** Fire `work-decision-commit` once on `workflow_dispatch` after merge and read the run log; a green empty run is the evidence it can reach the VM.
3. `WO-20260901-PHASE-H` is `in_flight` and its answer to `DEC-20260901-READ-GATE-SEQUENCING` decides whether the read gate is built at all.
